best_for: Developers and curious tinkerers with a 16 GB machine who want to try open-weight language models offline, or serve them to their own code through a local API.

points.title: Run models on your own machine
points.text: LM Studio finds and downloads models from Hugging Face inside the app and runs GGUF models through llama.cpp, plus MLX models on Apple Silicon. Once a model is downloaded, it can run fully offline.

points.title: A local API for your code
points.text: It can serve loaded models on OpenAI-compatible endpoints, on your computer or across your network. The `lms` command-line tool and a headless server build cover scripts and CI, and it can connect to MCP servers.

points.title: Chat with your documents
points.text: You can attach files to a chat for retrieval done on your machine, so documents need not go to a cloud service.

points.title: Free app, paid cloud extras
points.text: The Free plan covers local models, offline voice transcription and LM Link on up to 5 devices. Bionic+ at USD 20 per month and Pro at USD 100 per month add hosted models, more devices and higher usage. Prices were read on the date below.

points.title: Closed source
points.text: The terms grant use for personal and internal business purposes and treat the source code as a trade secret. The Flathub listing shows a proprietary license and is not marked verified.

points.title: Hardware matters
points.text: Macs need Apple Silicon and macOS 14 or later; Intel Macs are not supported. On Windows, x64 CPUs need AVX2, and the docs recommend 16 GB of RAM and 4 GB of dedicated video memory. Snapdragon X Arm PCs are supported.

points.title: Versions kept here
points.text: The Windows listing keeps 70 versions, with x64 and Arm64 installers in per-user and machine-wide forms. macOS and Linux list only the current release, so downgrades there need another source.
